repository.description: A managed, orchestrated harness for running Claude Code as a safe, repeatable agent: hooks, guardrails, slash commands, a Jira CLI, and a cross-session handover system.
repository.name: Himmel
repository.readme:
# himmel

> **A harness for Claude Code.**

> 🚀 **New here? → [Getting Started](docs/getting-started.md)** — clone to your
> first PR-gated loop in ~15 minutes.
>
> Deciding whether it is worth it? → [**Why himmel**](docs/why-himmel.md) — the
> failure modes it exists for, and what each one costs. Want the wiring? →
> [**Architecture**](docs/architecture.md) — the enforcement layers, handover,
> fleet, Jira seam, and observability chain as diagrams.

A solo-operator / small-team development engine. Ships CLIs, hooks, plugins,
and Claude Code wiring designed for a worktree-isolated, PR-gated, Jira-tracked
workflow with a strong dose of AI assistance.

himmel is the **engine**: the tools that automate the parts a single operator
would otherwise repeat by hand (commit hooks, Claude session guardrails, handover
state, Jira sync, overnight unattended runs).

> **Companion second-brain (optional).** himmel pairs naturally with an AI-first
> Obsidian vault that Claude reads and writes directly — the Camp-2 memory
> substrate described below. himmel ships a ready-to-use template at
> [`templates/luna-second-brain/`](templates/luna-second-brain/) to bootstrap one.
> Cross-session handover state lives under your own repo (or an external handover
> repo via `$HANDOVER_DIR`) — see the
> [handover system](docs/internals/handover-system.md).

## What you get

The payoff of running Claude Code through himmel rather than bare:

- **Work compounds across sessions.** Durable markdown handover state means you
  never re-explain context — a fresh session resumes exactly where the last one
  stopped, with the decisions intact (not just *what* shipped, but *why*).
- **Unattended overnight execution.** `/overnight-shift` dispatches scoped tickets
  as parallel agents that branch, self-review, and open PRs while you sleep;
  on approaching a usage cap, the auto-arm-on-cap watchdog "arms" a scheduled
  relaunch — an OS scheduler task that restarts the session — so a long run
  survives it.
- **Mistakes are structurally hard, not just discouraged.** Guardrail hooks block
  edits on `main`, secret reads, and opening a PR without a passing review — at the
  tool-call layer. Correctness lives in the structure, not in Claude remembering a
  rule.
- **Multi-agent review before every merge.** `/pr-check` runs a panel of review
  agents plus a cross-model first pass and gates the PR on a clean result —
  with an adversarial verify-before-critical rule to kill hallucinated findings.
- **Token-cheap by construction.** A local Jira CLI instead of an MCP (Model
  Context Protocol) server, an
  output-summarizing CLI proxy, and lean per-subagent context briefs keep the
  context window (and the bill) small.
- **Memory you can read and edit by hand.** A plain-markdown Camp-2 substrate
  (the two-camps taxonomy is unpacked in
  [Memory architecture](#memory-architecture--camp-2-a-context-substrate-not-a-backend)
  below) with no opaque memory backend — the only index (qmd, BM25 + vectors) is a derived,
  disposable view that always points back at the source files, never a
  replacement for them.
- **Forge-agnostic.** The worktree→PR→merge loop, PR review threads, and
  luna-ingest work the same on GitHub or Bitbucket Cloud — the backend is chosen
  per-repo from the `origin` remote, so nothing in the day-to-day loop changes.
- **Linux and macOS supported.** Linux is CI-gated on every PR; macOS is
  verified on the nightly only; Windows / Git Bash / WSL are not supported
  in v1.0.0. See [Support matrix](#support-matrix).

## Quickstart

himmel is a harness *for* [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code), so you
need Claude Code installed (`curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash`, or
`irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex` on Windows) either way.

Two ways to get himmel — pick based on what you're doing:

1. **Add himmel to an existing repo** (most common) — the portable core: hooks
   + guardrails + worktree workflow + marketplace plugins/skills. Follow
   [`docs/getting-started.md`](docs/getting-started.md) for the ~15-minute
   walkthrough instead of this section, or see the eight-level
   [adoption trail](docs/adoption-trail.html) for what each stage of adoption
   changes (also at
   [yotamleo.github.io/Himmel/adoption-trail.html](https://yotamleo.github.io/Himmel/adoption-trail.html)).
2. **Run / develop himmel standalone** — the contributor path, heavier
   prereqs. The rest of this Quickstart documents this path.

Prereqs: `bash`, `git`, `node`, `npm`, `bun`, `python3`, `jq`, `gh`, `mktemp` —
verified as foundational tools by `scripts/setup.sh` step `[0/9]` (fails fast
with install hints if any are missing) — plus **one of `uv`, `pipx`, or a
pre-installed `pre-commit`**: step `[1/9]` hard-exits if none of the three is
present (step `[0/9]` does not check for them). `pre-commit` itself is
**not** a prerequisite you need pre-installed: `scripts/setup.sh` installs it
itself at step `[1/9]` (via `uv`/`pipx`) and wires the git hooks (pre-commit,
pre-push, commit-msg) at step `[2/9]`. `bun` runs the handover armed-resume
resolver, the qmd search index, the Telegram bridge, and the obsidian-triage
tools. See
[`docs/setup/new-machine.md`](docs/setup/new-machine.md) for the per-platform
shell-and-package install (Linux / macOS; its Windows Git Bash notes are
unsupported in v1.0.0, see the [Support matrix](#support-matrix)).

**Linux — from the release tarball (checksummed, pre-built, no clone, no `npm install`):**

```bash
V=X.Y.Z   # a release that ships the tarball: https://github.com/yotamleo/Himmel/releases
curl -fsSLO "https://github.com/yotamleo/Himmel/releases/download/v$V/himmel-$V-linux.tar.gz"
curl -fsSLO "https://github.com/yotamleo/Himmel/releases/download/v$V/himmel-$V-linux.tar.gz.sha256"
sha256sum -c "himmel-$V-linux.tar.gz.sha256" \
  && mkdir -p ~/.local/share/himmel/"$V" \
  && tar -xzf "himmel-$V-linux.tar.gz" -C ~/.local/share/himmel/"$V" --strip-components=1 \
  && ln -sfn "$V" ~/.local/share/himmel/current \
  && node ~/.local/share/himmel/current/scripts/himmelctl/bin.js install --scope user
```

The `&&` chain is the point: a tarball whose bytes do not match the published
`.sha256` fails `sha256sum -c` and nothing is extracted or installed. If you
have `gh`, you can additionally verify the tarball was built by this repo's
CI (optional — the hash check above is the mandatory step):
`gh attestation verify himmel-$V-linux.tar.gz -R yotamleo/Himmel`. Each
release lands in its own user-owned `~/.local/share/himmel/<version>/` (no
root), and `~/.local/share/himmel/current` points at the live one;
`himmelctl install` wires everything through `current` and puts a `himmelctl`
launcher in `~/.local/bin`. The tarball is built by CI on each `v*` tag
([`release.yml`](.github/workflows/release.yml)); the checksum is of that exact
built asset.

To upgrade, run `himmelctl update`: it downloads the latest release, verifies
its `.sha256` (and its attestation when `gh` is installed and logged in),
extracts it into a new `~/.local/share/himmel/<version>/` and only then swaps
`current` to it in one step. A download that fails to verify changes
nothing. The previous version stays in place. To roll back, run
`ln -sfn <previous-version> ~/.local/share/himmel/current`. After
`himmelctl uninstall`, removing `~/.local/share/himmel` removes every version.
An install from an earlier recipe (the tree extracted straight into
`~/.local/share/himmel`) predates this layout. Move it aside and install once
with the recipe above.

**Any platform — from a clone:**

```bash
git clone https://github.com/yotamleo/Himmel himmel
cd himmel
node scripts/himmelctl/bin.js install
```

Node-less machine? Bootstrap first: `bash scripts/himmelctl/bootstrap.sh`
(Windows, unsupported in v1.0.0: `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\himmelctl\bootstrap.ps1`), then re-run
`install`. Under the hood the wizard runs `scripts/setup.sh` /
`scripts\setup.ps1` (Windows, unsupported in v1.0.0) for this standalone
path — invoke those directly for the manual or CI path.

Minimum environment (set in the shell that launches Claude or your daily
work shell):

luna, telegram, hermes, and Jira are all optional — the harness runs without them.

| Variable             | Required? | Notes                                                              |
|----------------------|-----------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `USER_SLUG`          | recommended | Your kebab-case handle — e.g. `jane-doe`. Names your handover bucket (`handovers/<USER_SLUG>/`) and worktree dirs. If unset, auto-derived from your slugified `git config user.name`; setup fails only if both are unset. |

## Usage — the core loop

Day-to-day work runs through one PR-gated loop, driven by slash commands inside
a Claude Code session:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["/worktree feat/x"] --> B["work with Claude"]
    B --> C["commit + push"]
    C --> D["/pr-check"]
    D -->|clean| E["gh pr create / gh pr merge"]
    E --> F["/clean"]
    F --> G["/handover"]
```

```bash
/worktree feat/my-thing   # isolated branch + git worktree (never edit on main)
#   … work with Claude in the worktree …
git commit && git push    # commit-msg gate; pre-push gates write the CR (code-review-owed) marker
/pr-check                 # multi-agent review; clears the merge gate when clean
#   gh pr create / gh pr merge --squash   # PR-gated; ≥1 approval to merge
/clean                    # prune merged-PR worktrees
/handover                 # snapshot state so the next session resumes here
```

Going unattended:

```bash
/overnight-shift --limit 5   # dispatch 5 scoped tickets as parallel agents → PRs
/stop                     # graceful halt marker for an in-flight overnight run
```

The narrated walkthrough — every hook and gate explained at the point it fires —
is in [`docs/daily-loop.md`](docs/daily-loop.md). The full control surface —
every chain, gate (HARD vs auth-gated vs advisory), knob, and off switch in one
place — is [`docs/configuration.md`](docs/configuration.md). Working LLMs (or a
new session) should start from [`llms.txt`](llms.txt), the machine-readable map
of the repo.

## Who is this for — Tier 3-4 on the maturity ladder

Claude Code use spans four maturity tiers: **Tier 1 vanilla** (out-of-the-box —
notably where Boris Cherny, a creator of Claude Code, has described his own
setup as "surprisingly vanilla"), **Tier 2 customized** (skills + slash
commands), **Tier 3 orchestrated** (parallel agents + harnesses), and **Tier 4
24/7 autonomous** (scheduled unattended runs).

himmel targets **Tier 3-4**. It is the harness that turns vanilla Claude Code
into an orchestrated, PR-gated, Jira-tracked, overnight-capable operator:
worktree isolation, multi-agent code review, guardrail hooks, handover state
that survives session boundaries, and `/overnight-shift` unattended dispatch.

If you are happy at Tier 1 — and many excellent engineers are — you do not need
himmel. It earns its complexity only once you run multiple parallel sessions,
want unattended overnight work, or need work to compound across sessions without
re-explaining context each time.

## Memory architecture — Camp 2 (a context substrate, not a backend)

himmel takes an explicit stance on agent memory. Following the two-camps
taxonomy (memory *backends* vs context *substrates*), himmel is firmly **Camp
2**: the handover system, AI-first markdown, and a companion AI-first vault
(the bundled [`templates/luna-second-brain/`](templates/luna-second-brain/)
template) **are** the memory — Claude reads those files directly, reasons
over them, and writes back, and the substrate compounds across sessions.
There is no memory **backend**: nothing extracts your files into a separate
store queried *instead of* the source. himmel does run a local search index
([qmd](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@tobilu/qmd) — BM25 + vectors) *over*
the same markdown, but it is a derived, drop-and-rebuild view that points
back at the real file, never a replacement for it — qmd embeds the files and
returns a pointer to the source, whereas a Camp 1 backend embeds extracted
facts and returns the fact in the file's place. That is the line, not
whether embeddings are used.

The reasoning: a single operator *is* the source of truth and can read/edit
the substrate by hand. Camp 1 (extract → embed → store → similarity-retrieve)
destroys exactly the structural context that makes compounding work — an
extracted fact instead of the whole file, its links, and the surrounding
decisions — and removes your ability to inspect and correct the memory. Camp
1 wins when the corpus is too large to load and inspection isn't needed
(enterprise document QA); that is not himmel's use case.

### Companion vault tooling (optional)

If you run the second-brain substrate as an Obsidian vault, himmel ships (and
pins) the tooling to operate it. All of it is optional — the core harness runs
without any of it.

- **[obsidian-triage](marketplace/plugins/obsidian-triage/README.md)** (shipped by
  himmel) — autonomous harvest → triage → synthesis → archive for Obsidian Web
  Clipper output: `/harvest-clips`, `/triage-clips`, `/synthesize-clips`,
  `/archive-clips`. Turns a clip inbox into a self-maintaining knowledge base.
- **[qmd](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@tobilu/qmd)** — a fast local search
  engine (BM25 + vector) over your markdown, exposed to Claude as an MCP server
  (`qmd@qmd`); the standalone CLI installs from himmel's qmd fork via
  `bash scripts/lib/qmd-bin.sh install` (run automatically by setup/adopt).
  This is the retrieval layer over the substrate; it indexes the files, it
  does not replace them (see above).
- **[claude-obsidian](https://github.com/yotamleo/claude-obsidian)** — a SHA-pinned
  fork of [AgriciDaniel/claude-obsidian](https://github.com/AgriciDaniel/claude-obsidian);
  skills for operating an Obsidian wiki vault: ingest, query, save, and **vault
  health / lint** (its `wiki-lint` skill).
- **[obsidian (kepano)](https://github.com/kepano/obsidian-skills)** — SHA-pinned;
  the `obsidian-markdown` skill for Obsidian-flavored-markdown syntax.

Separately, a scheduled vault-health pass (`/obsidian-health`, from the
`obsidian-second-brain` skill set) is armed on a **weekly** cadence (Sun 04:00) by
[`pipeline-cadence`](.claude/commands/pipeline-cadence.md).

## Contributing

See [`docs/contributing.md`](docs/contributing.md) for the contribution
workflow. TL;DR:

1. All work goes through a PR; main is protected.
2. Conventional commits: `type(scope): [HIMMEL-N ]message`.
3. Worktree-isolated branches (`/worktree <type>/<slug>`); never edit on `main`.
4. Pre-commit + pre-push hooks must pass.
5. New shell scripts include a smoke test (`scripts/<area>/test-<thing>.sh`).

## Project conventions

himmel uses Conventional Commits + Jira-ticket-in-subject for traceability.
The pre-commit framework enforces the format. Worktrees live under
`.claude/worktrees/` and follow `<type>/<slug>` (`feat`, `fix`, `chore`,
`docs`, `refactor`, `test`).

Detailed conventions — branch protection, force-push gates,
cross-platform attestation, headless-Claude billing rules — all live in
[`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md).

Went from 6 to 8 because 6 measured an 18m23s # slowest shard (3m18s fastest) — round-robin, not the count, dumped # the corpus's two heaviest suites onto one shard (719s of its 1065s); # replaying measured durations predicts 9.9m at 8 but 10.7m at 12, so # more shards isn't monotonically better — a duration-aware split is # the real fix (follow-up). shard: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8] runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }} continue-on-error: ${{ matrix.os != 'ubuntu-latest' }} # HIMMEL-3919: bound the job (default is 6 h; main-push runs share one # non-cancelling concurrency group, so one hung shard queued every later # main run). The cap is OS-dependent because the nightly SUITE_TIER_MODE=all # legs are far slower than the fast-tier push/PR runs: ubuntu shard 8 took # 35-38 min and windows shards 79-115 min (run 36579691044; 128 min in run # 36443339522). suite-durations.tsv is the fast tier only (~18 min slowest # shard). ubuntu 60 is ~1.7x the slowest nightly shard; windows 180 clears # the 128 min max. A timed-out job is `cancelled`, which continue-on-error # does not absorb, so a windows cap below its real duration would turn the # aggregate red every night. There are no macos rows in this matrix # (macos-cadence.yml / os-verify.yml carry their own 120). timeout-minutes: ${{ matrix.os == 'windows-latest' && 180 || 60 }} steps: # fetch-depth: 0 (not the default shallow clone) so --changed-since below # can resolve a pull_request's base SHA, which a depth-1 checkout of the # head ref does not carry. - uses: actions/checkout@v7 with: fetch-depth: 0 # arm-resume's non-dry-run cases exercise the real `at` scheduler backend, # which the supported runtime provides (HIMMEL-594 `ubuntu.sh` installs + # enables at/atd). GitHub's ubuntu image ships without `at`, so CI fell back # to the crontab path and ~2 arm-resume cases diverged from a real install. # Install + enable it on Linux so CI mirrors the supported runtime # (HIMMEL-619). Scoped to Linux: no-op on the nightly windows leg. # HIMMEL-2871: the runner image preinstalls third-party apt sources # (Google Chrome, Microsoft, Azure CLI) we never use; when one of those # goes inconsistent upstream, `apt-get update` exits 100 and this step # kills the whole job before any suite runs. Drop those lists first so # the update depends only on the Ubuntu archive we actually need. # No `.list`/`.sources` suffix on the glob: ubuntu-24.04 runner images # ship these as deb822 `.sources` files, not legacy one-line `.list` # files, and a suffix-anchored glob silently matched nothing. - name: Install + enable at/atd (Linux — arm-resume scheduler backend) if: runner.os == 'Linux' # HIMMEL-3919: a hung dpkg/apt lock held this step ~1.5 h. Each apt call # gets a `timeout` and a dpkg-lock wait so a lock fails fast and visibly # instead of blocking silently. HIMMEL-4073: worst case is the 2 min # plain install + 5 min refresh + 5 min retry = 12 min, so the step cap # is 13 (it was 10 when the whole step was refresh + install). timeout-minutes: 13 run: | started=$SECONDS trap 'echo "at/atd install: duration_seconds=$((SECONDS - started))"' EXIT sudo rm -f /etc/apt/sources.list.d/google-chrome* /etc/apt/sources.list.d/microsoft-* /etc/apt/sources.list.d/azure-cli* # HIMMEL-4073: try the plain install first (the runner's package # index is usually fresh enough); only a failure pays for an index # refresh and a retry. Each branch logs which path ran. if sudo timeout 120 apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=60 at; then echo "at/atd install: plain install succeeded, index refresh skipped" else echo "at/atd install: plain install failed, falling back to index refresh + retry" sudo timeout 300 apt-get update -o Acquire::Retries=3 -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=120 sudo timeout 300 apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=120 at fi sudo systemctl enable --now atd || sudo service atd start || true # HIMMEL-2742: same shape as HIMMEL-2587 (lanes-and-trust-suites) — a # suite in this corpus (test-wizard-luna-sections.sh) shells out to bun # and fails closed ("required test tool not found before PATH scrub: # bun") without it. Installing bun keeps that hermetic PATH-scrub case # under a runner check; a self-skip would exit 0 with nothing exercised. - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2 # HIMMEL-3193: the run step below now covers marketplace/ (root `.`), where # the obsidian-triage suites need js-yaml + playwright from # tools/node_modules. ensure-deps.sh installs them and exits non-zero on # ANY npm/network failure (no `|| true`, no continue-on-error), so a flaky # install fails THIS step loudly instead of surfacing as a dozen # unrelated suite reds. Pinned by test-run-shell-tests.sh Case 23f. - name: Install obsidian-triage tool deps (marketplace suites) run: bash marketplace/plugins/obsidian-triage/tools/ensure-deps.sh # HIMMEL-2223 codex-3: scripts/test-template-nostash-hooks.sh hard-SKIPs # (exit 0) without pre-commit on PATH — the exact vacuous-SKIP shape # called out for the Windows vault suites above (LUNA-131) — so without # this install the suite is a permanent no-op here, never exercising the # real fixer hooks. `shell: bash` matches the Windows install pattern # above: python -m pip works identically on every OS in this matrix. - name: Install pre-commit (scripts/test-template-nostash-hooks.sh) shell: bash run: python -m pip install --disable-pip-version-check pre-commit # Explicit `bash` prefix: on windows-latest the default run shell is pwsh, # but Git Bash is preinstalled + on PATH, so `bash …` runs under MSYS2. # FAIL_LOG_DIR: full failed-suite logs land there and upload as an # artifact below — the inline tail is bounded, so without this the # failing assertion can be unrecoverable from Actions logs (HIMMEL-963). # SUITE_TIER_MODE (HIMMEL-2166): fast on every per-PR/post-merge leg # (pull_request, push, or a plain workflow_dispatch) — this job is # ubuntu-only there. `all` stays the corpus on the nightly leg that # expands to the paid windows matrix, matching the # cadence/full-scan intent this ticket must not touch. # SUITE_CHANGED_SINCE: only on pull_request, where a base SHA exists — # a docs-only PR then skips the whole corpus (run-shell-tests.sh's own # docs-only fast lane); push/schedule/dispatch have no PR base to diff. # Scan root `.` (HIMMEL-3193) = scripts/ + templates/ + marketplace/; the # duration ledger keys all three, so the bin-pack balances across them. # SUITE_IMPACTED_FROM_BASE (HIMMEL-3897): on a pull_request to the default # branch, the shards run only the suites the BASE commit's # scripts/ci/impacted-selection.sh selects for the PR diff — or the full # sweep, which it decides for any trust-path change (this file, # run-shell-tests.sh, the selector, the trust list), a base that is not on # main (spec hole H1), or any doubt. A PR to another branch, push, schedule # and dispatch pass '' = the full sweep. The 8 shards stay 8 required # contexts either way; a docs-only PR's shards exit 0 with nothing to run. # SUITE_MANIFEST: the selection this shard acted on and every suite's fate, # uploaded below and verified by the shell-unit aggregator. - run: bash scripts/ci/run-shell-tests.sh --shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/8 . env: FAIL_LOG_DIR: failed-suite-logs SUITE_TIER_MODE: ${{ github.event_name == 'schedule' && 'all' || 'fast' }} SUITE_CHANGED_SINCE: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.base.sha || '' }} SUITE_IMPACTED_FROM_BASE: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.base.ref == github.event.repository.default_branch && github.event.pull_request.base.sha || '' }} SUITE_MANIFEST: shard-manifest/manifest-shard${{ matrix.shard }}.txt - name: Upload shard manifest if: always() uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7 with: name: shell-unit-manifest-${{ matrix.os }}-shard${{ matrix.shard }} path: shard-manifest/ if-no-files-found: ignore retention-days: 14 # A re-run shard replaces its manifest, so the aggregator reads the # latest attempt's. overwrite: true - name: Upload failed-suite logs if: failure() || cancelled() uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7 with: name: shell-unit-failed-logs-${{ matrix.os }}-shard${{ matrix.shard }} path: failed-suite-logs/ if-no-files-found: ignore retention-days: 14 # LUNA-131 soak/sweeper suites — DORMANT in the private repo (HIMMEL-297: # CI lives on the public side). Kept here as reference/commented-out YAML, # not wired into any step — no `on:` trigger reaches this block. Un-comment # only on the public repo once these suites are ready to gate there. # run-shell-tests.sh cannot reach these: it only discovers `test-*.sh`, so # no .ps1 suite is visible to it at all. # # HONEST SCOPE (preserved from the design, for when this is un-commented # on the public repo): the windows-latest leg of this job expands only # on `schedule` and carries continue-on-error, so the # two Windows steps below would be a SIGNAL, not a gate — the real gate # is the local run in the LUNA-131 build. The correlator step is # cross-platform and would run on every PR's ubuntu leg, making IT the # one real gate among the three. None of this fires here — the whole # block is inert YAML comments. # # The vault suites hard-SKIP without pre-commit (test-vault-git.ps1:16-21), # and a SKIP exits 0 — so without this install the Windows steps below # would be a permanent vacuous PASS (LUNA-131). # - name: Install pre-commit (Windows) # if: runner.os == 'Windows' # shell: bash # run: python -m pip install --disable-pip-version-check pre-commit # # - name: Vault sweeper suite (Windows only) # if: runner.os == 'Windows' # shell: bash # run: | # set -o pipefail # pwsh -NoProfile -File templates/luna-second-brain/scripts/test-vault-sweeper.ps1 | tee sweeper.log # if grep -q '^SKIP all' sweeper.log; then # echo "::error::vault-sweeper suite SKIPPED — a SKIP is not a pass"; exit 1 # fi # # - name: Foreground-window logger suite (Windows only) # if: runner.os == 'Windows' # shell: bash # run: | # set -o pipefail # pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts/observability/test-foreground-window-log.ps1 | tee focus.log # if grep -q '^SKIP all' focus.log; then # echo "::error::foreground-window-log suite SKIPPED — a SKIP is not a pass"; exit 1 # fi # # - name: Focus/tick correlator suite # run: node --test scripts/observability/focus-tick-correlate.test.mjs # Aggregating gate (HIMMEL-2872). Four things worth knowing before touching # this job: # # 1. The single-value `os` matrix below is deliberate and load-bearing: it # is what makes the check-run context `shell-unit (ubuntu-latest)` rather # than a bare `shell-unit`, keeping the required branch-protection # context byte-for-byte identical to what it was before the work above # was sharded. Sharding the work must not rename the gate. # 2. `needs.shell-unit-shard.result` is the matrix ROLLUP, `success` only # when every leg that CAN fail the matrix succeeded. A job-level # `continue-on-error` failure (the nightly windows leg) is NOT # counted against that rollup, so those legs stay advisory exactly as # they are today — this job never has to name any OS itself. # 3. `if: always()` plus the explicit `!= success` test below is the # fail-CLOSED shape: `failure`, `cancelled` AND `skipped` all redden this # job. A bare `needs:` without `always()` would SKIP this job whenever a # shard failed — and a required check that never reports leaves the PR # hanging rather than red. # 4. No setup: this job is a verdict, not work. It DOES check out (HIMMEL-3166) # — the report steps below run a repo script, and without a checkout # `bash scripts/ci/shell-extended-nightly-issue.sh` died with rc=127 on # the 2026-09-18 nightly, so the alert never fired. A plain checkout # rather than a sparse `scripts/ci` one: the script sources nothing today, # but this leg only runs unwatched, so a future `source` of a sibling lib # would re-break it silently. Same shape as bun-suites' windows-nightly # steps. # # 5. issues:write (beyond the workflow-level contents:read) is needed only # by the shell-extended-nightly-issue.sh steps below — scoped to this # job alone, same pattern as bun-suites' windows-nightly-issue.sh. # HIMMEL-3132: SUITE_TIER_DEFAULT `extended` suites only run under # SUITE_TIER_MODE=all (the schedule leg, set above at # shell-unit-shard), so a red extended suite only ever reddens THIS # job on that leg — a run nobody watches interactively. Without these # steps that failure is silent even though the job itself goes red. shell-unit: needs: shell-unit-shard if: always() # HIMMEL-3788: a manual dispatch on an arbitrary branch/PR head must not # post a check-run literally named "shell-unit (ubuntu-latest)" -- # identical to (and newer than) the PR's own required check -- or GitHub's # required-check evaluation and check-ci.sh both read the dispatch run's # result and shadow the PR's. HIMMEL-3853 removed the all-OS dispatch input, # so a dispatch is now ubuntu-only; the distinct name is kept as the # name-collision guard. # schedule/pull_request/push keep the unchanged name. name: shell-unit${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && ' (dispatch verify)' || '' }} (${{ matrix.os }}) permissions: contents: read issues: write strategy: matrix: os: [ubuntu-latest] runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }} steps: # Full history: impacted-selection.sh diffs base...HEAD and checks the # base is on origin/main, exactly as the shards did. - uses: actions/checkout@v7 with: fetch-depth: 0 - name: Every gating shell-unit shard must have passed env: SHARDS_RESULT: ${{ needs.shell-unit-shard.result }} run: | echo "shell-unit-shard matrix rollup: $SHARDS_RESULT" if [ "$SHARDS_RESULT" != "success" ]; then echo "::error::shell-unit shards did not all pass (matrix rollup: $SHARDS_RESULT) — see the shell-unit-shard jobs on this run." exit 1 fi echo "OK: every gating shell-unit shard passed." - name: Download shard manifests if: ${{ !cancelled() }} uses: actions/download-artifact@v7 with: pattern: shell-unit-manifest-ubuntu-latest-shard* path: shard-manifest/ merge-multiple: true # HIMMEL-3897: green shards are not enough once a PR's shards run only # the impacted suites. Recompute the selection here (same base-sourced # script, same base, same merge commit) and require every ubuntu shard's # manifest to carry it verbatim, and the shards together to have run each # selected suite exactly once and green. A missing manifest, one from # another sha, or a shard that ran less than selected is red. The # aggregator's own `--list .` is the discovery a shard's `notfound` is # checked against: a suite it lists to RUN that no shard ran is red, so a # shard cannot drop one by filtering it or claiming notfound. Its tier and # changed-since filters MUST match the shards' env above (the impacted # filter stays off: the selection is checked separately). - name: Every shard ran exactly the selection env: IMPACTED_BASE: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.base.ref == github.event.repository.default_branch && github.event.pull_request.base.sha || '' }} SUITE_TIER_MODE: ${{ github.event_name == 'schedule' && 'all' || 'fast' }} SUITE_CHANGED_SINCE: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.base.sha || '' }} run: | bash scripts/ci/impacted-selection.sh "$IMPACTED_BASE" HEAD > shard-selection.txt head -n 2 shard-selection.txt bash scripts/ci/run-shell-tests.sh --list . > shard-discovered.txt bash scripts/ci/shard-manifest-verify.sh --dir shard-manifest --shards 8 --selection shard-selection.txt --discovered shard-discovered.txt # HIMMEL-3897 / HIMMEL-3896: the post-merge full sweep is where a # selector miss shows up — a suite red on main that the merged PR's # impacted selection did not list. Recorded, never blocking: the red # shards already fail this job; this names which reds a PR run would # have missed, for the selector's miss ledger. - name: Selector-miss ledger (main push, red sweep) if: failure() && github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' env: RANGE: ${{ github.event.before }}..${{ github.sha }} run: | awk '$1 == "ran" && $2 != "0" { print $3 }' shard-manifest/manifest-shard*.txt 2>/dev/null | sort -u > shard-red-suites.txt echo "red suites on this sweep: $(wc -l < shard-red-suites.txt)" rc=0 bash scripts/cr/impacted-suites.sh --selector-miss "$RANGE" --red-file shard-red-suites.txt > selector-miss.txt || rc=$? { echo "### Selector-miss ledger ($RANGE, rc $rc)"; echo '```'; cat selector-miss.txt; echo '```'; } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY" cat selector-miss.txt - name: Upload selector-miss ledger if: failure() && github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7 with: name: selector-miss-ledger path: | selector-miss.txt shard-red-suites.txt if-no-files-found: ignore retention-days: 90 # Scoped to the schedule leg: that is the only leg where # SUITE_TIER_MODE=all actually exercises the extended tier (see # shell-unit-shard above), so only there does a red here plausibly mean # an extended suite broke rather than double-reporting a per-PR fast- # tier failure the PR gate already surfaced. - name: Extended-tier nightly issue — clear on green if: success() && github.event_name == 'schedule' env: GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }} run: bash scripts/ci/shell-extended-nightly-issue.sh 0 "${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}" - name: Extended-tier nightly issue — file/refresh on red if: failure() && github.event_name == 'schedule' env: GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }} run: bash scripts/ci/shell-extended-nightly-issue.sh 1 "${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}"

# himmel

> **A harness for Claude Code.**

> 🚀 **New here? → [Getting Started](docs/getting-started.md)** — clone to your
> first PR-gated loop in ~15 minutes.
>
> Deciding whether it is worth it? → [**Why himmel**](docs/why-himmel.md) — the
> failure modes it exists for, and what each one costs. Want the wiring? →
> [**Architecture**](docs/architecture.md) — the enforcement layers, handover,
> fleet, Jira seam, and observability chain as diagrams.

A solo-operator / small-team development engine. Ships CLIs, hooks, plugins,
and Claude Code wiring designed for a worktree-isolated, PR-gated, Jira-tracked
workflow with a strong dose of AI assistance.

himmel is the **engine**: the tools that automate the parts a single operator
would otherwise repeat by hand (commit hooks, Claude session guardrails, handover
state, Jira sync, overnight unattended runs).

> **Companion second-brain (optional).** himmel pairs naturally with an AI-first
> Obsidian vault that Claude reads and writes directly — the Camp-2 memory
> substrate described below. himmel ships a ready-to-use template at
> [`templates/luna-second-brain/`](templates/luna-second-brain/) to bootstrap one.
> Cross-session handover state lives under your own repo (or an external handover
> repo via `$HANDOVER_DIR`) — see the
> [handover system](docs/internals/handover-system.md).

## What you get

The payoff of running Claude Code through himmel rather than bare:

- **Work compounds across sessions.** Durable markdown handover state means you
  never re-explain context — a fresh session resumes exactly where the last one
  stopped, with the decisions intact (not just *what* shipped, but *why*).
- **Unattended overnight execution.** `/overnight-shift` dispatches scoped tickets
  as parallel agents that branch, self-review, and open PRs while you sleep;
  on approaching a usage cap, the auto-arm-on-cap watchdog "arms" a scheduled
  relaunch — an OS scheduler task that restarts the session — so a long run
  survives it.
- **Mistakes are structurally hard, not just discouraged.** Guardrail hooks block
  edits on `main`, secret reads, and opening a PR without a passing review — at the
  tool-call layer. Correctness lives in the structure, not in Claude remembering a
  rule.
- **Multi-agent review before every merge.** `/pr-check` runs a panel of review
  agents plus a cross-model first pass and gates the PR on a clean result —
  with an adversarial verify-before-critical rule to kill hallucinated findings.
- **Token-cheap by construction.** A local Jira CLI instead of an MCP (Model
  Context Protocol) server, an
  output-summarizing CLI proxy, and lean per-subagent context briefs keep the
  context window (and the bill) small.
- **Memory you can read and edit by hand.** A plain-markdown Camp-2 substrate
  (the two-camps taxonomy is unpacked in
  [Memory architecture](#memory-architecture--camp-2-a-context-substrate-not-a-backend)
  below) with no opaque memory backend — the only index (qmd, BM25 + vectors) is a derived,
  disposable view that always points back at the source files, never a
  replacement for them.
- **Forge-agnostic.** The worktree→PR→merge loop, PR review threads, and
  luna-ingest work the same on GitHub or Bitbucket Cloud — the backend is chosen
  per-repo from the `origin` remote, so nothing in the day-to-day loop changes.
- **Linux and macOS supported.** Linux is CI-gated on every PR; macOS is
  verified on the nightly only; Windows / Git Bash / WSL are not supported
  in v1.0.0. See [Support matrix](#support-matrix).

## Quickstart

himmel is a harness *for* [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code), so you
need Claude Code installed (`curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash`, or
`irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex` on Windows) either way.

Two ways to get himmel — pick based on what you're doing:

1. **Add himmel to an existing repo** (most common) — the portable core: hooks
   + guardrails + worktree workflow + marketplace plugins/skills. Follow
   [`docs/getting-started.md`](docs/getting-started.md) for the ~15-minute
   walkthrough instead of this section, or see the eight-level
   [adoption trail](docs/adoption-trail.html) for what each stage of adoption
   changes (also at
   [yotamleo.github.io/Himmel/adoption-trail.html](https://yotamleo.github.io/Himmel/adoption-trail.html)).
2. **Run / develop himmel standalone** — the contributor path, heavier
   prereqs. The rest of this Quickstart documents this path.

Prereqs: `bash`, `git`, `node`, `npm`, `bun`, `python3`, `jq`, `gh`, `mktemp` —
verified as foundational tools by `scripts/setup.sh` step `[0/9]` (fails fast
with install hints if any are missing) — plus **one of `uv`, `pipx`, or a
pre-installed `pre-commit`**: step `[1/9]` hard-exits if none of the three is
present (step `[0/9]` does not check for them). `pre-commit` itself is
**not** a prerequisite you need pre-installed: `scripts/setup.sh` installs it
itself at step `[1/9]` (via `uv`/`pipx`) and wires the git hooks (pre-commit,
pre-push, commit-msg) at step `[2/9]`. `bun` runs the handover armed-resume
resolver, the qmd search index, the Telegram bridge, and the obsidian-triage
tools. See
[`docs/setup/new-machine.md`](docs/setup/new-machine.md) for the per-platform
shell-and-package install (Linux / macOS; its Windows Git Bash notes are
unsupported in v1.0.0, see the [Support matrix](#support-matrix)).

**Linux — from the release tarball (checksummed, pre-built, no clone, no `npm install`):**

```bash
V=X.Y.Z   # a release that ships the tarball: https://github.com/yotamleo/Himmel/releases
curl -fsSLO "https://github.com/yotamleo/Himmel/releases/download/v$V/himmel-$V-linux.tar.gz"
curl -fsSLO "https://github.com/yotamleo/Himmel/releases/download/v$V/himmel-$V-linux.tar.gz.sha256"
sha256sum -c "himmel-$V-linux.tar.gz.sha256" \
  && mkdir -p ~/.local/share/himmel/"$V" \
  && tar -xzf "himmel-$V-linux.tar.gz" -C ~/.local/share/himmel/"$V" --strip-components=1 \
  && ln -sfn "$V" ~/.local/share/himmel/current \
  && node ~/.local/share/himmel/current/scripts/himmelctl/bin.js install --scope user
```

The `&&` chain is the point: a tarball whose bytes do not match the published
`.sha256` fails `sha256sum -c` and nothing is extracted or installed. If you
have `gh`, you can additionally verify the tarball was built by this repo's
CI (optional — the hash check above is the mandatory step):
`gh attestation verify himmel-$V-linux.tar.gz -R yotamleo/Himmel`. Each
release lands in its own user-owned `~/.local/share/himmel/<version>/` (no
root), and `~/.local/share/himmel/current` points at the live one;
`himmelctl install` wires everything through `current` and puts a `himmelctl`
launcher in `~/.local/bin`. The tarball is built by CI on each `v*` tag
([`release.yml`](.github/workflows/release.yml)); the checksum is of that exact
built asset.

To upgrade, run `himmelctl update`: it downloads the latest release, verifies
its `.sha256` (and its attestation when `gh` is installed and logged in),
extracts it into a new `~/.local/share/himmel/<version>/` and only then swaps
`current` to it in one step. A download that fails to verify changes
nothing. The previous version stays in place. To roll back, run
`ln -sfn <previous-version> ~/.local/share/himmel/current`. After
`himmelctl uninstall`, removing `~/.local/share/himmel` removes every version.
An install from an earlier recipe (the tree extracted straight into
`~/.local/share/himmel`) predates this layout. Move it aside and install once
with the recipe above.

**Any platform — from a clone:**

```bash
git clone https://github.com/yotamleo/Himmel himmel
cd himmel
node scripts/himmelctl/bin.js install
```

Node-less machine? Bootstrap first: `bash scripts/himmelctl/bootstrap.sh`
(Windows, unsupported in v1.0.0: `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\himmelctl\bootstrap.ps1`), then re-run
`install`. Under the hood the wizard runs `scripts/setup.sh` /
`scripts\setup.ps1` (Windows, unsupported in v1.0.0) for this standalone
path — invoke those directly for the manual or CI path.

Minimum environment (set in the shell that launches Claude or your daily
work shell):

luna, telegram, hermes, and Jira are all optional — the harness runs without them.

| Variable             | Required? | Notes                                                              |
|----------------------|-----------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `USER_SLUG`          | recommended | Your kebab-case handle — e.g. `jane-doe`. Names your handover bucket (`handovers/<USER_SLUG>/`) and worktree dirs. If unset, auto-derived from your slugified `git config user.name`; setup fails only if both are unset. |
| `JIRA_PROJECT_KEY`   | required only for Jira ops | e.g. `HIMMEL`. The project the CLI creates/queries issues in. |
| `JIRA_BASE_URL`      | required only for Jira ops | Your Atlassian site, e.g. `https://your-site.atlassian.net`. |
| `JIRA_API_TOKEN` + `JIRA_EMAIL` | required only for Jira ops | API-token credentials. Never commit. `.env` is gitignored. |
| `HANDOVER_DIR`       | recommended | Path to your external handover repo (Mode B). See handover docs. Unset it and run `/handover-setup` once instead — a fresh clone has no handover root until then, and `handover_root` fails closed with a diagnostic rather than crashing or writing to the wrong place. |

The local Jira CLI needs only those four (`JIRA_BASE_URL`, `JIRA_EMAIL`,
`JIRA_API_TOKEN`, `JIRA_PROJECT_KEY`) — **no cloud ID**. `JIRA_CLOUD_ID` is
only for the optional Atlassian MCP server (Confluence and a few ops the CLI
lacks), not the CLI; `ORGANIZATION_ID` is legacy — nothing reads it today.
Full list: [`.env.example`](.env.example).

After setup, sanity-check the install:

```bash
node scripts/jira/dist/index.js list      # talk to Jira
gh auth status                            # talk to GitHub
pre-commit run --all-files                # all hooks green
```

Then run one full loop end-to-end — worktree → commit → PR → merge →
`/clean` → `/handover`, with every hook and gate explained at the point it
fires: [`docs/daily-loop.md`](docs/daily-loop.md).

## Usage — the core loop

Day-to-day work runs through one PR-gated loop, driven by slash commands inside
a Claude Code session:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["/worktree feat/x"] --> B["work with Claude"]
    B --> C["commit + push"]
    C --> D["/pr-check"]
    D -->|clean| E["gh pr create / gh pr merge"]
    E --> F["/clean"]
    F --> G["/handover"]
```

```bash
/worktree feat/my-thing   # isolated branch + git worktree (never edit on main)
#   … work with Claude in the worktree …
git commit && git push    # commit-msg gate; pre-push gates write the CR (code-review-owed) marker
/pr-check                 # multi-agent review; clears the merge gate when clean
#   gh pr create / gh pr merge --squash   # PR-gated; ≥1 approval to merge
/clean                    # prune merged-PR worktrees
/handover                 # snapshot state so the next session resumes here
```

Going unattended:

```bash
/overnight-shift --limit 5   # dispatch 5 scoped tickets as parallel agents → PRs
/stop                     # graceful halt marker for an in-flight overnight run
```

The narrated walkthrough — every hook and gate explained at the point it fires —
is in [`docs/daily-loop.md`](docs/daily-loop.md). The full control surface —
every chain, gate (HARD vs auth-gated vs advisory), knob, and off switch in one
place — is [`docs/configuration.md`](docs/configuration.md). Working LLMs (or a
new session) should start from [`llms.txt`](llms.txt), the machine-readable map
of the repo.

## Who is this for — Tier 3-4 on the maturity ladder

Claude Code use spans four maturity tiers: **Tier 1 vanilla** (out-of-the-box —
notably where Boris Cherny, a creator of Claude Code, has described his own
setup as "surprisingly vanilla"), **Tier 2 customized** (skills + slash
commands), **Tier 3 orchestrated** (parallel agents + harnesses), and **Tier 4
24/7 autonomous** (scheduled unattended runs).

himmel targets **Tier 3-4**. It is the harness that turns vanilla Claude Code
into an orchestrated, PR-gated, Jira-tracked, overnight-capable operator:
worktree isolation, multi-agent code review, guardrail hooks, handover state
that survives session boundaries, and `/overnight-shift` unattended dispatch.

If you are happy at Tier 1 — and many excellent engineers are — you do not need
himmel. It earns its complexity only once you run multiple parallel sessions,
want unattended overnight work, or need work to compound across sessions without
re-explaining context each time.

## Memory architecture — Camp 2 (a context substrate, not a backend)

himmel takes an explicit stance on agent memory. Following the two-camps
taxonomy (memory *backends* vs context *substrates*), himmel is firmly **Camp
2**: the handover system, AI-first markdown, and a companion AI-first vault
(the bundled [`templates/luna-second-brain/`](templates/luna-second-brain/)
template) **are** the memory — Claude reads those files directly, reasons
over them, and writes back, and the substrate compounds across sessions.
There is no memory **backend**: nothing extracts your files into a separate
store queried *instead of* the source. himmel does run a local search index
([qmd](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@tobilu/qmd) — BM25 + vectors) *over*
the same markdown, but it is a derived, drop-and-rebuild view that points
back at the real file, never a replacement for it — qmd embeds the files and
returns a pointer to the source, whereas a Camp 1 backend embeds extracted
facts and returns the fact in the file's place. That is the line, not
whether embeddings are used.

The reasoning: a single operator *is* the source of truth and can read/edit
the substrate by hand. Camp 1 (extract → embed → store → similarity-retrieve)
destroys exactly the structural context that makes compounding work — an
extracted fact instead of the whole file, its links, and the surrounding
decisions — and removes your ability to inspect and correct the memory. Camp
1 wins when the corpus is too large to load and inspection isn't needed
(enterprise document QA); that is not himmel's use case.

### Companion vault tooling (optional)

If you run the second-brain substrate as an Obsidian vault, himmel ships (and
pins) the tooling to operate it. All of it is optional — the core harness runs
without any of it.

- **[obsidian-triage](marketplace/plugins/obsidian-triage/README.md)** (shipped by
  himmel) — autonomous harvest → triage → synthesis → archive for Obsidian Web
  Clipper output: `/harvest-clips`, `/triage-clips`, `/synthesize-clips`,
  `/archive-clips`. Turns a clip inbox into a self-maintaining knowledge base.
- **[qmd](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@tobilu/qmd)** — a fast local search
  engine (BM25 + vector) over your markdown, exposed to Claude as an MCP server
  (`qmd@qmd`); the standalone CLI installs from himmel's qmd fork via
  `bash scripts/lib/qmd-bin.sh install` (run automatically by setup/adopt).
  This is the retrieval layer over the substrate; it indexes the files, it
  does not replace them (see above).
- **[claude-obsidian](https://github.com/yotamleo/claude-obsidian)** — a SHA-pinned
  fork of [AgriciDaniel/claude-obsidian](https://github.com/AgriciDaniel/claude-obsidian);
  skills for operating an Obsidian wiki vault: ingest, query, save, and **vault
  health / lint** (its `wiki-lint` skill).
- **[obsidian (kepano)](https://github.com/kepano/obsidian-skills)** — SHA-pinned;
  the `obsidian-markdown` skill for Obsidian-flavored-markdown syntax.

Separately, a scheduled vault-health pass (`/obsidian-health`, from the
`obsidian-second-brain` skill set) is armed on a **weekly** cadence (Sun 04:00) by
[`pipeline-cadence`](.claude/commands/pipeline-cadence.md).

## Contributing

See [`docs/contributing.md`](docs/contributing.md) for the contribution
workflow. TL;DR:

1. All work goes through a PR; main is protected.
2. Conventional commits: `type(scope): [HIMMEL-N ]message`.
3. Worktree-isolated branches (`/worktree <type>/<slug>`); never edit on `main`.
4. Pre-commit + pre-push hooks must pass.
5. New shell scripts include a smoke test (`scripts/<area>/test-<thing>.sh`).

## Project conventions

himmel uses Conventional Commits + Jira-ticket-in-subject for traceability.
The pre-commit framework enforces the format. Worktrees live under
`.claude/worktrees/` and follow `<type>/<slug>` (`feat`, `fix`, `chore`,
`docs`, `refactor`, `test`).

Detailed conventions — branch protection, force-push gates,
cross-platform attestation, headless-Claude billing rules — all live in
[`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md).
